name: Aloo Amritsari
ingredients: 4 medium potatoes (Yukon Gold or Russet), boiled with skin, cooled
2 tbsp gram flour (besan), roasted until fragrant
1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder (for color)
1 tsp pomegranate seed powder (anardana), for tang
instructions: 1. Gently peel the boiled potatoes and cut them into wedges or thick slices. 2. In a bowl, mix gram flour, all spice powders, ajwain, dry mango powder, black salt, and regular salt. 3. Add mustard oil and water a teaspoon at a time to form a thick, coating-like paste. 4. Toss the potato wedges in this paste, ensuring each piece is well-coated. 5. If using a tandoor: skewer the potatoes and cook at high heat (500°F) for 8-10 minutes, turning once, until charred spots appear. Alternatively, bake at 450°F on a wire rack for 15-20 minutes, broiling the last 2 minutes. 6. Baste with melted butter or ghee if desired, and sprinkle with pomegranate powder and fresh cilantro. 7. Serve hot with mint chutney or tamarind sauce.
description: A symphony of earthy potatoes and tangy pomegranate, kissed by the smoke of tandoor and the warmth of Punjabi spices.
